title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Bound Record. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Bound Record
options.lineage: the bound analytical report — numbered method, ruled results, struck-through corrections, an appendix of raw data
options.thesis: Every claim carries its method, in the one document form where that is the grammar rather than a feature.
options.viewport: A numbered section head, a wide ruled results table, and a hairline margin column carrying the provenance of every figure beside it.
options.risk: A record can read as inert. It must feel like an instrument being used, not an archive being stored.
options.case: The document already half-is this: an evidence ledger, corrections stated in place rather than deleted, and a known-issues line. This makes the whole surface behave the way its best part already does.

options.label: Departures Board
options.lineage: rail concourse split-flap board — fixed columns, ranked rows, amber for exception
options.thesis: The 114 ideas as a live departures board: columns never move, rows re-rank, a failed gate reads like a cancelled train.
options.case: Wins audience identification outright — Boeing, concourses, public information. Loses product clarity: fixed-column grammar owns the scorecard and has nothing to say about thirteen sections of argued prose.
options.viewport: The scorecard as the board: eight fixed columns, rows cascading into rank order.
options.risk: Two thirds of the document is prose, and prose on a departures board is a costume.

options.label: Datamatics
options.lineage: Ryoji Ikeda — hairline bar fields, monospace numerics, full-frame inversion
options.thesis: 193,600 combinations rendered as the field they are, and your one choice as a single lit column inside it.
options.case: Fuses poorly on a named fact: the grammar forbids colour, and this product needs a five-step score ramp and four axis colours that carry meaning and are contrast-verified in both themes. Stripping them would fail an accessibility check, not just a taste one.
options.viewport: A wall of hairline columns, one of them yours.
options.risk: Beautiful, and it deletes the colour system three harnesses currently verify.

options.label: Deck Fascia
options.lineage: cassette-futurist tape deck — engraved labels, panel grid, amber ladders
options.thesis: One fascia holds everything: every function gets its own labelled switch, and the score climbs an amber ladder.
options.case: Fuses honestly — a tool with four modes really is a panel of labelled zones, and the axis picker really is a bank of switches. Weakest on craft risk: brushed metal and lit LEDs are exactly the chrome the quality floor treats as a substitute for authored content.
options.viewport: A bolted panel: mode zones left to right, the picker as switch banks, meters along the foot.
options.risk: Skeuomorphism ages badly and the metal is a texture, not an idea.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The analytics dashboard, executed impeccably — neutral ground, one blue accent, cards, a sidebar.
canonCard.viewport: What you would expect, at full craft and nothing more.
canonCard.risk: You would not be able to tell it from any other tool, which for a private instrument may be exactly fine.
